title: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization
meta_description: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization exists because a specific failure keeps repeating: customer truth is scattered across product silos, channels and vendors; personalization runs on segments built quarters ago, and privacy governance arrives as an afterthought that blocks launches.
Customer truth is scattered across product silos, channels and vendors; personalization runs on segments built quarters ago, and privacy governance arrives as an afterthought that blocks launches.

The pattern behind Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization: decisions that should be systematized are still assembled by hand — one document, one queue, one meeting at a time. This solution replaces the assembly with a governed composition.

We build the identity spine first (consent-scoped, clean-room-ready), unify behavioral, transactional and service data with certified definitions, then wire decision APIs for next-best-action into every channel with measurement that proves incrementality.
Named modules with a gate at each boundary — Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization edition:

items: durable IDs, consent scopes and preference management
streaming unification with certified customer definitions
next-best-action, offers and timing served in the moment
profiling governance designed before the first campaign

blocks.title: From signal to decision to evidence — Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization
blocks.note: Named stages, not generic boxes — this is the Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization path as built.

blocks.x: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization composes Dataq Nexus, Dataq Forge — platforms with documented controls and evidence packs, so governance is part of the runtime. The pattern is in delivery now in Retail & Consumer Goods, Banking & Financial Services, Telecom, Media & Entertainment, Insurance & Risk.

Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization runs on phases: phase one prices the problem in your own units and signs the baseline; phase two designs with the risk envelope written down; phase three proves a bounded slice on your data; phase four scales what survived the gate. Baselines are signed in the first two weeks, the working slice lands inside the quarter, and the value ledger stays open to your finance team. For Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization, that discipline is not optional — it is the engagement model.
The Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization value case names what should move and by what mechanism. The numbers get filled in from your baseline, not from a brochure.
Bring Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization to a 45-minute briefing with the practice lead — your metric, our method, and an honest read on feasibility.
